primary_sources.title: On rotated backwards self-similar solutions of the incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes equations

verified_interfaces.PV_G: smooth NSE on B1×[-1,0), pointwise local Type-I |u|<=C_u/(sqrt(-t)+|x|), annular pressure L∞, and one sufficiently late time with small self-similar generator ∂_s U (L∞ or the weighted L1 alternative) imply regularity at (0,0).
verified_interfaces.PV_E: Proposition 9.5 consumes a late one-slice critical enstrophy smallness condition. Footnote 27 explicitly permits replacing the annular-pressure assumption by the assumption that (u,p) is a suitable weak solution in Q1 satisfying the same pointwise Type-I bound.
verified_interfaces.pressure_bifurcation: The annular pressure is not merely cosmetic in the PV_G proof as written: the proof uses it at the selected time to obtain annular/bulk pressure and Bernoulli bounds before the weighted identity (9.20)-(9.25). Suitability is an explicit alternative only for the downstream PV_E criterion.

primary_sources.title: On local Type I singularities of the Navier-Stokes equations and Liouville theorems
locators: Lemma 2.2 and persistence package as source-bound in RAKL_math PR #110

verified_interfaces.producer: finite I is the scale-critical local A+C+D+E ledger used in the Type-I suitable-weak / bounded-ancient equivalence; stronger pointwise/weak-Serrin Type-I bounds can imply finite I, but the converse is not licensed.
verified_interfaces.compactness: the registered local compactness interface is strong L3_loc convergence of velocity and weak L3/2_loc convergence of pressure on fixed smaller cylinders; this does not transport annular L∞ pressure, ∂_t u, ∇u time traces, or the one-slice generator.

direct_derivations.self_similar_generator: U(y,s)=sqrt(-t)u(x,t), y=x/sqrt(-t), s=-log(-t); then ∂_s U=sqrt(-t)[(-t)∂_t u-(1/2)u-(1/2)(x·∇)u].
direct_derivations.PV_E_singularity_floor: If the PV_E consumer hypotheses hold and (0,0) is singular, then for every sufficiently late admissible time t, with r=sqrt(-t), r∫_{B_{2R** r}}|ω(x,t)|²dx > θ_*²/4; otherwise Proposition 9.5 would imply regularity.
direct_derivations.finite_I_good_time_upper_bound: Assume additionally finite I and fix r>0. Put ρ=2R**r. The finite-I E-ledger gives ∫_{-ρ²}^0∫_{B_ρ}|∇u|²<=Iρ. Averaging on t∈[-r²,-r²/2] gives a t_* with r_*=sqrt(-t_*)∈[r/sqrt(2),r] and r_*∫_{B_{2R**r_*}}|ω|²<=8R** I. Thus finite I gives O(I), not the source epsilon threshold unless I is correspondingly small.
direct_derivations.singular_subclass_I_lower_bound: Under the PV_E singularity floor, integrate on t∈[-r0²,0], use |ω|²<=2|∇u|² and B_{2R**sqrt(-t)}⊂B_{2R**r0}. Then ∫_{-r0²}^0∫_{B_{2R**r0}}|∇u|² >= θ_*² r0/4, whereas finite I gives at most 2R** I r0; hence any such singular solution must satisfy I>=θ_*²/(8R**). This is a scoped corollary, not a regularity theorem.
direct_derivations.compact_orbit_falsifier: Precompactness of a trajectory does not imply liminf ||∂_s U||=0: an abstract periodic orbit s↦(cos s,sin s) is compact and has unit speed. Therefore a critical-element route needs an additional finite-action/Lyapunov/no-recurrence witness before it can feed PV_G.

limit_and_rigidity_audit.weak_strong: AB strong L3_loc velocity is adequate for local nonlinear passage but does not control derivatives or one-time generator traces; weak L3/2_loc pressure is weaker than the PV_G annular L∞ hypothesis.
limit_and_rigidity_audit.pressure_localization: Local Calderón–Zygmund plus harmonic-remainder control is sufficient for suitable-weak/local epsilon-regularity but not the PV_G annular/bulk pointwise pressure estimates used in (9.17)-(9.25). Switching to PV_E avoids that pressure interface if suitability is available.
limit_and_rigidity_audit.far_field: PV_E is genuinely local and does not require the global critical tail that blocked PR #110; this is why R6/PR110 failures changed routing. No global tail conclusion is inferred.
limit_and_rigidity_audit.noncompact_symmetries: translation/dilation/profile leakage remains relevant to global critical-element constructions. Rotation/self-similar-time periodicity is an additional recurrence obstruction for generator-smallness.
limit_and_rigidity_audit.backward_uniqueness: not used by PV_E/PV_G. No unique-continuation hypotheses are imported.
limit_and_rigidity_audit.equation_change: this atom remains Type-I Navier–Stokes. Type-II Euler limits are rejected as a transfer source for this interface.

exact_missing_interfaces.generic_finite_I_to_PV_E: prove pointwise local Type-I plus a sufficiently late one-slice critical-enstrophy dip, or replace PV_E by a theorem whose input is exactly finite I/suitable weak.
exact_missing_interfaces.critical_element_to_PV_G: prove annular pressure at the needed strength and liminf_{s→∞} A(s)=0, where A(s) is the PV weighted generator action; a sufficient stronger bridge is finite total weighted generator action in self-similar time.
exact_missing_interfaces.subclass_next_atom: NS-B1b1a1: within suitable weak solutions already satisfying the pointwise local Type-I bound, test whether NSE dynamics/geometric depletion/local enstrophy evolution can force the PV_E one-slice epsilon dip without small-I.
